full_judgment: 12. A suit can be defeated by reason of misjoinder and non-joinder of parties. Objection as to non-joinder or misjoinder of parties must be taken at the earliest opportunity. In the present case, the trial Court found that the suit is not bad for defect of parties. The trial Court held that the fact that the suit is bad for defect of parties was not agitated by the defendant, either in their written statement nor before the trial Court and since objection as to non- joinder or misjoinder of parties was not taken at the earliest possible opportunity such objection cannot be taken subsequently and such right of the defendant shall be deemed to have been waived. Order I, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that no suit shall be defeated by reason of misjoinder or non-joinder of parties and rule 13 of the said Order provides that all the objections on the grounds of non-joinder or misjoinder shall be taken at the earliest possible opportunity and any such objection not so taken shall be deemed to have been waived.
